q: A researcher records how children play at recess without interacting with them or changing anything. Which method is this?
exp: Observing behavior in a natural setting without controlling it is naturalistic observation.
why: "Case study" means: A descriptive method that examines one individual or group in depth.
"Survey" means: A descriptive technique used to get the self-reported attitudes and behaviors of a particular group, usually by questioning a representative random sample of the group.
An experiment manipulates a variable; here nothing is changed.

q: Students who miss more school tend to have lower grades. This is a:
exp: One goes up while the other goes down: negative. It still doesn't prove absences cause the lower grades.
why: "Positive correlation" means: Two variables increase or decrease together. Examples from your slides: as sleep increases, memory increases; as salary decreases, spending also decreases; as hourly pay increases, employee morale increases.
"Zero (no) correlation" means: No relationship between the two variables. On a scatterplot, the dots are scattered with no pattern.
A correlation can't prove cause and effect.

q: A study tests whether caffeine improves memory. One group gets caffeine, the other gets none, then both take a memory test. What is the dependent variable?
exp: The DV is what's measured. Caffeine is the IV (what the researcher changes).
why: Caffeine is what the researcher changes: the independent variable.
That's the control group, not a variable that's measured.
That's the sample size, not the outcome being measured.

q: In the caffeine study, the group that gets no caffeine is the:
exp: The control group doesn't receive the manipulated variable, so it can be compared with the experimental group.
why: "Experimental group" means: Participants who receive the manipulated variable. Example from your slides: the group that takes the antidepressant.
"Population" means: The group that the research is meant to apply to.

"Confounding variable" means: An outside influence that affects the results of the study. Example from your slides: when studying how exercise (IV) affects weight loss (DV), possible confounding variables are diet, amount of sleep, and genetic issues.

q: Factory workers become more productive just because they know researchers are watching them. This is the:
exp: Changing behavior because you know you're being observed is the Hawthorne effect.
why: "Placebo effect" means: Experimental results caused by expectations alone. Example: participants act or claim to feel a certain way because they think they received a drug that would cause that reaction.

"Barnum effect" means: Believing that personality descriptions apply specifically to you (more than to other people), even though the description is filled with information that applies to everyone. Example: your horoscope.
"Gambler's fallacy" means: The tendency to overestimate the occurrence of patterns in random data.

q: After the game, Sam says, "I knew they would lose all along." This is:
exp: Believing after the outcome that you would have foreseen it is hindsight bias.
why: "Overconfidence" means: The tendency to overestimate your knowledge and/or ability.
"Gambler's fallacy" means: The tendency to overestimate the occurrence of patterns in random data.
"Social desirability bias" means: People giving answers that may be dishonest because they are seeking approval and/or want to highlight their character strengths.

q: After an experiment, participants are told the study's real purpose and about any deception. This is called:
exp: Debriefing happens after the study. Informed consent happens before.
why: "Informed consent" means: Giving potential participants enough information about the study to let them choose whether or not to participate.
"Confidentiality" means: Participants' information is kept private.
Replication means repeating a study to see if the results hold.

q: On an anonymous-looking survey about cheating, almost no students admit to cheating, even though many do. The most likely problem is:
exp: People give dishonest answers to seek approval or look good.
why: "Hawthorne effect" means: Participants changing their behavior because they know they are being observed.

"Placebo effect" means: Experimental results caused by expectations alone. Example: participants act or claim to feel a certain way because they think they received a drug that would cause that reaction.
"Gambler's fallacy" means: The tendency to overestimate the occurrence of patterns in random data.

q: Mr. Epstein gives his students candy to reward them for doing their homework. Which perspective fits best?
exp: Rewarding a behavior so it gets repeated is the behavioral perspective.
why: "Cognitive perspective" means: How our internal thought processes shape our behavior. Emphasizes memory, problem solving, intelligence, and perception.

"Humanistic perspective" means: How humans can achieve their full potential, emphasizing free will, self-efficacy, and self-actualization. Also emphasizes relationships, positivity, and maximizing well-being.
"Psychodynamic perspective" means: Behavior is influenced by your unconscious mind and past experiences, especially those from childhood. Based heavily on the ideas of Freud.

q: Doctors believe Rosa suffers from schizophrenia because there is too much dopamine in her brain. Which perspective fits best?
exp: Neurotransmitters like dopamine belong to the biological perspective.
why: "Psychodynamic perspective" means: Behavior is influenced by your unconscious mind and past experiences, especially those from childhood. Based heavily on the ideas of Freud.
"Sociocultural perspective" means: Humans behave and act differently based on the influences of their culture or way of life.
"Evolutionary perspective" means: Human behavior is a result of evolutionary processes that protect us, give us adaptive behaviors, and help us be more successful at reproducing.

q: Alex is learning to focus on positive relationships and his future potential, instead of the past, to improve his self-esteem. Which perspective fits best?
exp: Potential, positivity, and relationships are humanistic. Focusing on the past would be psychodynamic.
why: "Psychodynamic perspective" means: Behavior is influenced by your unconscious mind and past experiences, especially those from childhood. Based heavily on the ideas of Freud.
"Behavioral perspective" means: How our behaviors have been influenced by our learned experiences. We often repeat behaviors that are reinforced by positive rewards.
"Biological perspective" means: The importance of genetics, brain chemistry, hormones, and neurotransmitters (like dopamine and serotonin) in influencing behavior and thinking.

q: What is the mean of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10?
why: 5 is the number of scores, not their average.
8 is one of the scores; the sum (30) ÷ 5 is 6.
4 is one of the scores; the sum (30) ÷ 5 is 6.

q: What is the median of 3, 9, 1, 7, 5?
exp: In order: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The middle number is 5.
why: "The scientific method (7 steps)" means: 1. Observe some aspect of the universe. 2. Develop a theory. 3. Use the theory to make a hypothesis. 4. Test the predictions with experiments, using operational definitions. 5. Evaluate the results. 6. Modify the theory in light of your findings. 7. Replicate.
9 is the highest score; put them in order and take the middle one.
"3 key principles" means: 1. Representative samples are better than unrepresentative samples. 2. Bigger samples are better than small ones. 3. More estimates are better than fewer estimates.

q: What is the mode of 4, 7, 7, 2, 9, 7, 4?
exp: 7 appears three times, more than any other number.
why: 4 appears twice; 7 appears three times.
9 appears only once.
2 appears only once.

q: Test scores: 60, 72, 85, 90, 95. What is the range?
exp: 95 − 60 = 35. (80.4 is the mean, a trap.)
why: 80.4 is the mean, not the range.
85 is the median, not the range.
Range is highest minus lowest: 95 − 60, not 85 − 60.

q: On a very hard test, most students score low, but a few score very high. The distribution is:
exp: The few high scores make a tail to the right: positive skew.
why: Negative skew has its tail on the left, from a few very low scores.
"Symmetrical distribution" means: No skew: mean = median = mode.
"Bimodal curve" means: A graph with two peaks ("bi" means two). Each peak is a local maximum: the highest values compared with the data points right around them.

q: On a very easy quiz, most students score near 100, but a few score very low. How does the mean compare to the median?
opts: The mean is lower than the median
The mean is higher than the median
exp: The tail goes left (negative skew), and the mean follows the tail.
why: The few low scores pull the mean down, not up.
They're equal only in a symmetrical distribution.
Every set of numbers has a mean.

q: A study finds p = .03. What does this mean?
opts: The result is statistically significant: it's unlikely to be due to chance
exp: p ≤ .05 is statistically significant. A p-value says nothing about how strong the effect is; that's effect size.
why: p ≤ .05 counts as significant, and .03 is below .05.
A p-value doesn't measure strength; effect size does.
A p-value isn't a percentage of participants.

q: Jada scored in the 90th percentile on a practice test. This means:
opts: She scored higher than 90% of test takers
She got 90% of the questions right
She scored 90 points above the mean
exp: Percentile rank is the percentage of scores below yours.
why: Percentile compares you with other test takers, not with the number of questions.
Percentile isn't a count of test takers.
Percentile isn't a point score.
